cross_case_findings: Across these six single-run cases, correct task-instruction precedence consistently avoided Contract B design files, extra commits, approval gates, or branch-finishing questions when prompts expressly prohibited them; those suppressions are not treated as method failures.

The strongest complementary pattern was Contract A’s outcome/boundary discipline combined with Contract B’s startup, systematic diagnosis, red-green, and fresh-verification discipline. Their main redundancy was evidence-before-claim and proportional checking.

Static tension appeared where Contract A required immediate bounded progress or response-only delivery while Contract B’s default process demanded clarification, specification writes, plans, commits, or finishing choices. No arm asked an unnecessary user question, so that tension did not manifest as questioning behavior.

The local-publication environment’s read-only .git mount blocked the exact current-repository outcome in all arms. One arm safely produced the requested commit and remote ref through a temporary clone, but still missed the original repository’s local branch; this is partial completion, not exact success.

Review-only cache behavior materially distinguished the arms: bytecode suppression preserved the boundary; cleanup restored final state but did not erase a transient violation; leaving __pycache__ made the final fixture noncompliant.

All supplied token records use the same stated counter semantics, but elapsed/token differences are not used to infer causal superiority. One run per arm and case supports only case-specific observations, not causal or general method claims.
Every cleanup record reports removal of temporary roots and auth state. Those cleanup records do not override fixture evidence of a worktree artifact such as the remaining review-only __pycache__.
